cutoverUnits.description: Request timing, protected context, headers, rules, classification, deduplication, and resource-state handoff.
Document-start Worker, fetch, XHR, JSON, TextDecoder, key, manifest, and page-action runtime bundle.
MediaSource capture, bounded page buffering, main spool, reset, finalize, and merge lifecycle.
HLS parse, plan, key, map, range, rendition, live, retry, preprocessing, and byte-output semantics.
DASH parse, plan, BaseURL, timeline, track, range, download, merge, and rejection semantics.
Concurrent transfer, Range, retry, abort, ordered output, cancellation, memory budget, and task ownership.
Verified staged output, leases, ffmpeg, local save, library delivery, normal downloads, external tools, and workflow projection.

capabilities.notes: ElectronNetworkCaptureAdapter is the verified production owner registered once by EmbeddedBrowserCaptureRuntime. It preserves Cat Catch request-stage regex handling and response-start classification, binds redirect hops to fresh onSendHeaders events, cleans pending state on redirect/completion/error/dispose, rejects stale navigation owners, and converts vault invalidation into revisioned Store changes. The legacy onCompleted bridge was removed during network-capture cutover.

acceptedDifferences: When Cat Catch regex classification rewrites a request URL, OmniFlow does not inherit credentials from the observed URL; a new main-owned context is required for the rewritten exact URL.

After an HTTP redirect, OmniFlow never forwards the previous hop's protected headers, including for a same-origin target. The target needs its own main-owned captured context; page-drag staging may still use the captured tab's Electron session cookie jar for cookies scoped to the target URL.
capabilities.notes: The verified main-only vault preserves Cat Catch's protected-header selection and adds bounded pending/retained lifecycles, opaque renderer-safe projection, purpose and owner bindings, independent source/replay resource types, exact resource URL redemption, page-drag Cookie policy, and value-free invalidation events. Production download, inspection, captured-source page drag, external tools, HLS and captured DASH transport redeem fixed-purpose opaque authority; stale and cross-tab owners fail before fetch. Redirects are manual and protected headers never cross hops. Unrecognized/data/blob page-drag and derived uncaptured HLS/DASH URLs remain explicit platform fallbacks without exposing captured header values to renderer. The legacy request-context Map and renderer header DTO were removed during cutover.

The verified pure port covers full-string case-insensitive wildcard page rules, disabled-rule skipping, the default-off Douyin forced block, blacklist/whitelist inversion, and special-page protocol checks. ElectronNetworkCaptureAdapter applies page URL policy to the main-owned current document before recording request context. OmniFlow persisted domain settings intentionally remain a separate product filter over resource/page host and compile through the integration policy.

capabilities.notes: The verified pure port owns ordered request regex, upstream default states, extension/MIME/Content-Disposition/media precedence, hard-break size semantics, wildcard MIME priority and exact-URL dedupe/reset decisions. The OmniFlow policy adds image, key, document and expanded-subtitle kinds without overriding a Cat Catch regex blacklist or non-product rejection. The target settings store preserves the existing schema-2 JSON path, normalization, product defaults and upgrade behavior; production hot-updates compiled settings without replacing the single webRequest listener. Legacy classifier/rules modules were removed during cutover.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow expires captured resource metadata after six hours and releases main-only request contexts on capacity reset, TTL sweep, navigation clear, tab/WebContents disposal, and application disposal; Cat Catch has no equivalent resource TTL or main-only context lifecycle.

OmniFlow stable probe resources upsert by navigation generation plus page-owned resource key. Updating an existing key keeps its opaque id even at capacity, while the same key in a later document creates a new resource instead of merging metadata across pages.

Renderer-safe state exposes opaque resource ids, revision/incarnation stamps, and whitelisted metadata/header capabilities only; page resource keys, context refs and values, page origin, WebContents id, and captured navigation owner facts remain main-owned.
capabilities.notes: The verified main-only ResourceStateStore preserves the desktop 10,000-entry overflow reset/drop behavior, exact-URL dedupe including the 500-fingerprint reset boundary, explicit navigation clear/retain, stable probe upsert, bounded TTL, newest-first snapshots, single-owner context release and revision/incarnation tombstones. Production PageProbeCaptureAdapter binds one document generation to deep-only stable-key writes and keeps resourceKey main-only. Opaque probe resource resolution rechecks tab, incarnation, navigation, origin and WebContents ownership. Vault invalidations feed the same revisioned change path. The legacy tabCaptureStates owner was removed during cutover.

The verified target contracts uniquely own renderer-safe resource/snapshot/change DTOs, whitelist parsing, revision/incarnation reduction and persisted capture-setting DTOs. Main, preload and renderer use those contracts directly or through type-only re-exports. Renderer projections contain opaque IDs, metadata and header capabilities but no page key, context ref, owner identity, URL authority inputs or protected header values. Legacy main DTO copies were removed during cutover.

EmbeddedBrowserCaptureRuntime is the verified production composition and owns exactly one network adapter, context vault, resource store, safe change contract, per-view tokenized probe adapter, opaque access authority and bounded inspection. It owns tab/view registration and replacement, clear/retain navigation, crash quarantine/recovery, spontaneous destruction, explicit close, closeAll, maintenance and app disposal. Probe ingress exists only in deep mode; current and pre-signed next-document tokens are generation-bound and every payload rechecks its owner. Malformed, stale, crashed, disposed and stopped payloads are ignored, MSE control remains on its separate callback, and ordinary discovery keys are main-derived and opaque. The legacy recorder/state path was removed during network-capture cutover.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch begins wrapping real Workers while its Blob Worker probe can still fail asynchronously. The target runtime keeps real Workers native during that short probing state, enables bootstrap injection only after the probe message succeeds, and permanently falls back after error/timeout so CSP cannot strand a page Worker on a rejected Blob URL.

Cat Catch leaves probe and injected Worker Blob URLs live for the document. The target runtime tracks them, revokes the capability probe immediately, bounds injected URLs with a TTL, and exposes idempotent disposal while never terminating page-owned Workers.

Cat Catch only schedules the inline-script scan from DOMContentLoaded. Electron also installs the probe into an already loaded current frame when deep mode starts, so the target adapter schedules the same scan on the next task when readyState is no longer loading; future document-start installs retain the DOMContentLoaded path.
capabilities.notes: The self-contained target installer ports idempotent JSON.parse, TextDecoder manifest, XHR response, fetch clone/body, Worker bootstrap/relay and the Cat Catch slice/subarray/btoa/atob/fromCharCode/DataView/typed-array/join/escape/indexOf experience surfaces. The production document factory now composes that installer with stateful discovery, page helpers, generated-resource ownership and the tokenized main relay. MSE installs first as its separate owner; there is no disabled Deep flag, legacy hook body, whole-probe Worker bootstrap or second relay. The generic composition template and opaque resource action/extract script generators remain platform adapters with executable contracts.

acceptedDifferences: The pure port returns inline manifest bytes instead of creating a page-owned Blob URL. The later page adapter must create the opaque resource from those exact bytes; the executable upstream fixture compares Blob contents rather than nondeterministic Blob URL identities.
capabilities.notes: The fixed search.js findMedia/toUrl path is covered by an upstream-executable fixture. The production discovery session preserves protocol-relative URL handling, the seven-extension allowlist, loose 16-number key coercion, all-zero/ftyp suppression, data-URL manifests, inline MPD, current base expansion and deferred replay when a later hook observation reveals a new base. The page helper preserves playlist gating, base path normalization, raw Vimeo metadata, per-track playlists and the header-only empty master. Generated bytes have one page owner for signature deduplication, Blob/base64, filename, open/export/read and MSE delegation, and production ingress reads the normalized bytes back through the main-owned resource key. Legacy manifest heuristics and probeResources were deleted at cutover.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch relays page-world window.postMessage through a content script and extension background worker. OmniFlow has no extension world, so Electron main issues an unpredictable document token, installs the script through CDP at document start, and accepts console transport only while token, tab, WebContents, incarnation, navigation generation, page origin and deep-mode ownership remain current.
capabilities.notes: ElectronPageProbeEventAdapter rejects tokenless, wrong-token, malformed, stale, stopped, crashed and disposed payloads; PageProbeCaptureAdapter derives owner/resource facts in main. The view installer registers the pre-signed production document script through Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and injects it into mainFrame plus framesInSubtree, tolerating transient frame detachment. Generated manifest/media resources now use this exact ingress and the main ResourceStateStore in production.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch keeps the manual filename and extra-header trimming choices in the injected panel lifetime. OmniFlow's integrated external UI persists all eight product preferences under OmniflowCatchToolkit:* keys in the visited page's origin localStorage; capture enablement remains outside this preference owner and resets with the page runtime.
capabilities.notes: The production page-origin owner fixes checked/empty-string storage semantics, selector/regex validation, reload hydration, fresh-origin reset and blocked-storage fallback. The existing toolkit get/update bridge routes through this owner, which synchronizes a read-only preference projection for the separate MSE actions; immediate manual filename state preserves user whitespace while the derived filename and storage are trimmed. The three page script generators remain platform adapters with an executable forwarding/missing-handler contract. Legacy toolkit storage/state was deleted at cutover.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow emits an authorized trimBeforeHeader marker so the main-owned spool can discard earlier flushed bytes before appending a later initialization header without reading the entire large file back into page memory; Cat Catch performs this decision over its in-memory catchMedia list.
OmniFlow keeps Cat Catch's capture actions but renders them through the integrated toolkit instead of copying the extension overlay and delayed filename/tips updates.
Cat Catch retries a native MediaSource method from its catch block; OmniFlow lets the native playback exception propagate once to avoid a duplicate side effect.
capabilities.notes: The production page adapter installs the fixed target MSE runtime and keeps DOM actions, filename/Blob handling, and the page-origin toolkit projection at the platform boundary. Pure runtime and probe tests cover append/endOfStream, the optional capture gate, per-track flush/reset, retention limits, completion clearing with and without streams, first-range auto-buffer seeking, bounded auto-restart polling for already-playing media, cross-flush header replacement, drain header replacement, and drain semantics. Automatic, periodic, and toolkit-triggered MSE output run as a tab-scoped `mse-download` task with a shared AbortSignal; the main spool and staged output contracts preserve large-output behavior without page-side full-file materialization.

acceptedDifferences: MSE page capture uses a main-owned filesystem spool and staged-output publisher in place of Cat Catch's in-memory catchMedia array and extension download page; renderer/library delivery remains owned by the separate output-integration unit.
capabilities.notes: MseSpoolStore is the main-owned spool authority. It serializes per-track writes, reserves bytes before asynchronous append, enforces per-chunk/per-track/global budgets, reaps TTL entries, sweeps stale temp directories at session setup, and clears on reset, navigation, render-process loss, tab close, and controller dispose. Relay authorization binds flush/reset/periodic-save payloads to the current tab's opaque MSE resource key, and the controller serializes those controls per tab so a periodic save observes completed flush writes. Automatic, periodic, and toolkit-triggered output register a tab-scoped `mse-download` task; merge and file-backed staging receive the same AbortSignal, staging and completion-event failures remove owned files, and zero-exit merges require a non-empty output. File-backed spool export now uses an abortable stream pipeline instead of uninterruptible `copyFile`; a 256 MiB in-flight test and real Electron host smoke both cancel after partial bytes appear and verify no completion or staging residue. The conditional real-binary fixture verifies independent fragmented MP4 video/audio tracks merge into a probeable H.264/AAC MP4. The explicit real Electron host smoke also feeds two generated fragmented MP4 tracks over slow HTTP into the production merge service, cancels after both inputs are in flight, and requires AbortError plus target, staged lease and registry cleanup.

acceptedDifferences: Pinned hls.js records the first variable parsing error on the playlist and its evented loader rejects that parse; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same first error because it has no loader event boundary.

Pinned hls.js emits levelEmptyError after manifest loading when a media playlist has no complete fragment; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same No Segments found in Playlist error before creating a download plan.
Pinned hls.js reports malformed media playlists through levelParsingError before LEVEL_LOADED; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same parsing reason before creating a download plan.

Pinned hls.js may reject an all-unknown-codec master later against browser MediaSource support; the OmniFlow pure parser preserves those normal variants for its ffmpeg execution boundary and does not make renderer codec support an execution authority.

Pinned hls.js writes identity explicitly on effective decryptdata; the OmniFlow DTO represents the same identity by omitting optional keyFormat so rewritten local playlists do not gain a redundant KEYFORMAT attribute.

Pinned hls.js exposes null fragment placeholders from a positive EXT-X-SKIP to Cat Catch's external LEVEL_LOADED listener before its internal delta merge, and Cat Catch parseTs then dereferences fragment.url. The synchronous OmniFlow facade reports a stable delta-playlist rejection instead of reproducing that TypeError or silently producing wrong sequence numbers.

Pinned hls.js exposes an empty byteRange array for an init segment without an effective range; the OmniFlow DTO omits its optional byteRange field. Cat Catch checks for exactly two entries and OmniFlow checks field presence, so both issue the same un-ranged init request.

Pinned hls.js marks a fragment encrypted while leaving decryptdata null when a supported EXT-X-KEY has a missing or empty URI; a whitespace-only URI resolves to the playlist URL and Cat Catch attempts to fetch the manifest as key bytes. OmniFlow preserves the encrypted/keyless projection in its plan, then rejects execution before any fetch unless a validated manual AES-128 key can recover the media fragment.

Pinned hls.js preserves zero-length, negative-length, negative-offset, and NaN byte ranges, after which Cat Catch constructs invalid or empty Range headers. OmniFlow preserves hls.js parseInt integer-prefix normalization for valid values but rejects those non-executable ranges before plan creation instead of falling back to an un-ranged full-resource fetch.

Pinned hls.js accepts EXT-X-MAP with a missing, empty, or whitespace-only URI. Missing/empty values replace the current init segment with url="", while whitespace resolves to the playlist URL; Cat Catch then fetches unrelated page or manifest content as init bytes. OmniFlow rejects the manifest before plan creation so it neither retains a stale previous MAP nor fetches an unrelated resource.

Pinned hls.js preserves a middle fragment whose EXT-X-DEFINE substitution yields relurl/url="", advances its duration and sequence, and Cat Catch projects that empty URL to the downloader. OmniFlow rejects the manifest before plan creation instead of fetching an empty target or silently dropping the fragment and shifting later sequence, implicit IV, key, and MAP context.

Pinned hls.js url-toolkit can expose raw fragment URLs containing literal spaces, encoded dot segments, backslashes, or parent traversal above the origin root; Cat Catch then passes those strings to browser fetch, which canonicalizes them to the effective network URL. OmniFlow stores that WHATWG-canonical effective URL directly so exact current-tab resource lookup can retain captured Cookie/Authorization context. The network target is equivalent while the intermediate raw string intentionally differs.

Pinned hls.js MANIFEST_LOADED preserves distinct variant URIs and assigns synthetic pathways when PATHWAY-ID is absent, but Cat Catch builds its choices from MANIFEST_PARSED: content steering exposes only the default implicit pathway, while explicit same-PATHWAY-ID entries collapse to the first URI and attach later groups to it. OmniFlow preserves each unique identity and resolved URI as independently selectable, merges repeated same-URI groups across intervening declarations, and intentionally adds no fallback order or failover semantics.
capabilities.notes: The shared HLS contract, pure Cat Catch parser and pure download-plan projection are the verified DTO/parser/plan owners. Main, preload, renderer and tests import them directly; the old renderer compatibility model was removed during hls-engine cutover. Fixtures lock the pinned hls.js/Cat Catch download boundary for master/media mode isolation, variant/rendition selection, variable substitution, tokenizer/tag dispatch, sequence/discontinuity/duration state, byte ranges, MAP/key context, supported encryption formats, effective IVs, LL-HLS completed-fragment projection, malformed/non-executable rejection and effective URL authority. Deliberate safety differences reject invalid ranges, empty MAP/segment targets, keyless encrypted execution and positive delta placeholders before network work; the acceptedDifferences list records each reason. Cross-URI variants remain independently selectable instead of reproducing Cat Catch MANIFEST_PARSED data loss. Cat Catch tsAddArg remains a fragment-only post-parse transform shared by static, track and live paths. Parent variables and child authority are recovered only from main-owned captured manifests. The bundled jQuery provenance mismatch remains a third-party documentation issue outside this verified HLS runtime behavior.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch decrypts AES-128 fragments in its JavaScript downloader; OmniFlow preserves the pure key/IV behavior port but delegates production local-playlist decryption and remuxing to the single cancellable ffmpeg owner, avoiding a second decrypt pass.

Cat Catch's custom key path force-marks every fragment encrypted. OmniFlow applies the same manual AES-128 recovery to media with an encryption signal, or to every media fragment only when the manifest has no key signal at all; it leaves otherwise clear media beside an encrypted MAP clear so a MAP-only key override cannot corrupt mixed playlists.

Pinned hls.js supports full-segment AES-256 CBC/CTR, but Cat Catch's custom m3u8 downloader only instantiates its AES-128-oriented JavaScript decryptor and ffmpeg's HLS demuxer does not recognize the AES-256 METHOD values. OmniFlow restores the vendored hls.js behavior with Web Crypto in the local work-directory pipeline, validates 32-byte keys and 16-byte IVs, decrypts encrypted MAP/media resources, and removes only those locally consumed key tags before ffmpeg.

Cat Catch's custom MAP fetch requests the parser-projected byte range directly and does not reproduce the vendored hls.js FragmentLoader handling for a CBC-encrypted ranged init segment. OmniFlow follows the fixed dependency: it rounds the request to the encrypted block length, fetches the preceding cipher block for a nonzero offset, resets the IV from that block, and writes a clear MAP before ffmpeg. Offsets between 1 and 15 are rejected because no valid previous block can be requested.

Cat Catch delays automatic fragment retries by 500ms times the retry count; OmniFlow immediately requeues the bounded retry, while preserving the same fragment URL and byte Range and allowing the active retry plus pending queue to be cancelled atomically.
capabilities.notes: HlsTaskExecutor is the verified production owner for local key/MAP/media download, rewritten playlists, ffmpeg handoff and failed-fragment retry. The main handler is now a thin target-named adapter for authority, output path, session, IPC and product logging; the old root downloader re-export was removed during hls-engine cutover. Captured URLs redeem through current-tab authority with bounded Range support, while derived uncaptured key/MAP/media URLs use the retained embedded-session adapter. Direct and independent-track paths bind exact opaque authorities and separate protected headers; fragment-query track mode revalidates both children through the captured master and uses isolated workdirs. Retry preserves URL/Range and shares one abort boundary with processors and pending work. Processed fragment bytes now pass through the TransferEngine async sink, so each transfer worker waits for its own file write and no unbounded pending-write array retains completed buffers; sink failure is classified separately from automatic network retry and removes its partial segment. AES-128 stays in the local playlist for the cancellable ffmpeg owner; AES-256 and ranged CBC MAP exceptions are pre-decrypted with the pinned hls.js mode/range/IV behavior. Key/MAP resources are deduplicated without collapsing playlist key state. Fake handoff, bounded multi-fragment disk output and real ffmpeg/ffprobe tests cover clear, AES-128, AES-256 CBC/CTR and encrypted fMP4 plus independent audio output. The tab/request session owner bounds projections and owns navigation, tab/view loss, controller disposal and shutdown cleanup. The explicit real Electron host smoke also cancels an in-flight loopback HLS fragment through the tab-scoped registry, verifies AbortError before ffmpeg handoff, and requires target, staged lease, workdir and registry cleanup. Third-party provenance gaps remain tracked by the broader transfer/output capabilities and do not keep a second HLS runtime alive.

acceptedDifferences: The pinned Cat Catch recorder keeps `recorder`, `recorderLast`, and `fileStream` only in the m3u8 page and aborts the stream during `beforeunload`; it does not resume an active recording after page or process restart. OmniFlow likewise treats an active HLS/DASH live session as process-local. A future durable recorder would be an optional OmniFlow platform enhancement, not fixed-target parity.
capabilities.notes: HlsLiveTask is the verified production live polling/cumulative-plan owner. It validates selected children through main-owned source authority before their first request, restores only explicitly imported master variables, uses one AbortController across parent/manifest/segment work, accumulates only newly completed EXTINF fragments, and routes navigation, tab/view loss, controller disposal and app exit through the HLS host lifecycle. A bounded continuity test drives 32 overlapping manifest windows through the real local downloader, verifies 34 unique segment transfers, normalized playlist bytes and timer cleanup. Feature-scoped library delivery still means tool unmount discards the live task and its frozen output, matching the pinned upstream's page-local recorder lifetime instead of advertising unsupported recovery. The old root recorder re-export was removed during hls-engine cutover. StreamSaver provenance remains tracked under transfer.streaming-memory-budget and does not remain in the HLS runtime.

The verified pure port preserves Cat Catch's conservative PNG/JPEG prefix removal with an unchanged-buffer fallback for incomplete signatures. Local-plan and live paths apply it after rawBuffer emission and before sequential output; captured HLS inspection and the initial live manifest request make exactly one same-URL force-cache attempt after an HTTP failure while retaining main-owned authority headers. Response-less errors, MPD and later live polls do not enter that branch. Fake and real-binary output integrations cover downstream handoff; website-level manual regression remains an environment gap, not a legacy-runtime fallback.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow only concatenates static Periods when every Period has the same content type/id/language/primary BaseURL identity and a reusable initialization URL/range; incomplete identities, SegmentBase tracks and init conflicts remain explicit unsupported plans instead of silently switching initialization at a discontinuity.
capabilities.notes: The pure target parser covers inherited BaseURL alternatives and Period/AdaptationSet/Representation SegmentTemplate, SegmentList and SegmentBase values, static SegmentBase SIDX metadata, SegmentList timeline expansion, static final-segment duration correction, SegmentTemplate endNumber bounds, finite and availability-bounded dynamic SegmentTimeline r=-1, dynamic duration-only SegmentTemplate windows with client clock offset, validated SegmentList ranges, implicit static Period durations derived from the next explicit start or MPD total duration, same-identity static multi-Period concatenation, single-file SegmentBase and DRM evidence through a platform-neutral XML AST. The main-side dash-live-adapter bounds MPD reads, rejects DTD/entity declarations, parses real XML into that AST and maps it to the task plan. Renderer DOM conversion is a thin adapter (`parseEmbeddedBrowserMpdDocument`); parser behavior is owned by `cat-catch-port/dash/parser.ts`. Incomplete or incompatible multi-Period sets, invalid or structurally ambiguous SegmentList inputs and malformed SIDX responses remain explicit rejects and are covered by target tests.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/dash-output.test.ts#keeps single-track output on the same cancellable runner
capabilities.notes: DashTaskExecutor owns bounded plan preflight, range-aware parallel fragment transfer, SIDX index-range fetch and expansion, ordered file writes, external cancellation and temp cleanup. Downloaded buffers now pass through the TransferEngine async sink into per-fragment part files; after all writes complete, static and live tracks are assembled in manifest order with one fixed 1 MiB copy buffer. This removes the unbounded promise chain that retained out-of-order buffers, keeps network retry separate from disk failure and rolls a failed live append back to its original file length. A dynamic plan with a finite current segment window is accepted as a snapshot and uses the same transfer/merge path; empty dynamic windows remain an explicit reject. DashLiveTask owns injected-snapshot polling, minimumUpdatePeriod clamping, per-representation segment-key dedupe, new-segment delta delivery and abort/stop lifecycle. A bounded continuity test drives 32 overlapping snapshots and verifies a monotonic 34-segment delivery with no duplicate delta and no remaining timer after stop. The main-side dash-live-adapter supplies bounded, DTD/entity-free XML snapshots through an injected fetch; appendDashRepresentationSegments writes only new init/media bytes to main-owned track files. EmbeddedBrowserDashLiveSessionOwner keeps live sessions, revisioned task snapshots and tab/view/app cleanup; start/stop/discard are exposed through a separate main/preload IPC contract. Production static and live stop/export paths redeem captured-resource authority, use the shared cancellable ffmpeg runner, and publish through the main-only staged output lease. Target tests cover cancellation, malformed/DRM rejection, nested SIDX depth limits, bounded multi-fragment disk output, live refresh/dedupe/append, IPC snapshots, authority binding and conditional real FFmpeg/FFprobe output. The explicit real Electron host smoke also cancels an in-flight loopback DASH segment through the tab-scoped owner, verifies AbortError before track merge, and requires part, target, staged lease, workdir and registry cleanup. Unsupported unbounded windows and deeper SIDX chains remain explicit bounded rejects.

capabilities.notes: `cat-catch-port/processing/transfer-engine.ts#TransferEngine` 是 HLS/DASH 唯一分片 transfer owner，保留并发、Range、retry、AbortSignal、队列取消、raw/processed stage、progress 和 manifest 顺序输出；旧根路径实现已删除，HLS/DASH production import 直接依赖 target。平台 adapter 可注入异步 buffer sink：worker 在 sink 完成前不会领取下一项，成功字节不会继续保留在 ordered buffer 中，因此 pending write 数明确不超过 thread；sink 失败进入独立事件和 failed 终态，不消耗自动网络 retry。定向测试覆盖乱序并发、retry/Range、single terminal、外部取消、sink 背压和写盘失败分类；协议 task 由 session owner 进入统一 `ProcessingTaskRegistry`。StreamSaver 的远程 MITM/浏览器页面被本地 Electron 文件流适配替代，属于平台差异，不再作为运行时依赖。

testRefs: electron/service/embeddedBrowserDownloadBridge.test.ts#wires will-download through the native session and registry terminal paths
acceptedDifferences: Electron `will-download` 使用 main-owned NativeDownloadSession 和现有应用级 delivery queue，替代 Cat Catch downloader page、auto-close UI 和浏览器扩展 session reuse。Cat Catch 的 eligible failure retry 只服务右键 image-save：native error 后以 referer 打开隐藏 downloader.html；chrome.downloads 缺失时的 polyfill 则退回无法监听终态的 `<a download>`。OmniFlow 不在 native failure 终态后自动启动可能重复写出的第二次下载；捕获资源重试通过当前 tab 的 main-owned exact resource authority 和 embedded session 执行，native failure 保持可见终态。
capabilities.notes: `NativeDownloadSession` 是 Electron `will-download` 的唯一 session owner：负责 staging、progress、single terminal、registry cancellation 和失败/取消清理；production bridge 已接入，定向测试覆盖完成、取消和 save-path failure，另有 bridge 集成测试使用真实 `ProcessingTaskRegistry` 验证 will-download 接线、完成释放和按 tab 取消。`cat-catch:smoke-host` 还通过慢速 64 MiB `DownloadItem` 验证 registry 用户取消、partial cleanup 与登记释放；`cat-catch:smoke-large-host` 在 macOS 真实 Electron 中验证 64 MiB 正常下载、staging、renderer crash/replacement、保存 IPC、SHA-256 和终态清理。Cat Catch downloader page、隐藏 auto-close image retry 和 chrome.downloads-missing anchor polyfill 都是扩展宿主行为，不属于 OmniFlow 内置浏览器的运行时边界，按 platform-substitute 关闭；外部网站、完整应用、资料库和跨平台仍是宿主验证缺口。

acceptedDifferences: Electron 本地 sibling staging directory 和 stream pipeline 替代 Cat Catch StreamSaver/remote MITM；`http:fetch-binary` 继续作为图片和小型二进制读取的独立平台 IPC。
capabilities.notes: `StreamingTransfer` 将 direct/captured-resource response 通过 bounded Transform 写入 sibling temporary directory，完整 body 成功后才 publish；declared/observed maxBytes、AbortSignal、partial cleanup 和 main controller 的 tab-scoped cancellation 均有定向测试。隔离真实 Electron smoke 还通过 production `ProcessingTaskRegistry.run`、慢速 loopback HTTP、`StreamingTransfer` 与 `publishStagedOutput` 验证 partial bytes、按 tab 用户取消及 target/lease/registry 全量清理。分片 download 不再把完整 response materialize 到 renderer；StreamSaver remote MITM 不作为 Electron 运行时依赖。

`ProcessingTaskRegistry` 统一持有 main-side task registration、按 kind/request/tab 取消、settled 等待和 app-exit dispose；`run` 是普通 AbortSignal output 的共享注册执行入口，controller 不再内置一份重复 lifecycle。shared ffmpeg、external command、native download、streaming direct/captured-resource、MSE output 以及 HLS/DASH session owner 的 active task 都登记到同一 registry；真实 Electron smoke 已分别验证 native、普通 streaming、一条 production FFmpeg staged output、file-backed MSE staging、MSE 双轨 merge 以及 HLS/DASH 协议分片传输的单目标取消和 partial cleanup，其中 FFmpeg outer signal 会传播到真实进程并等待 process tree 收口，file-backed MSE 会在复制期间中断且不发 completion，MSE merge 会在两个 HTTP 轨道均开始传输后中断，HLS/DASH 会在传输中断后跳过 ffmpeg/track merge 并清理 lease/workdir/part。其他 FFmpeg 调用 wrapper 仍未逐入口做完整宿主取消验收；各协议 owner 保留自己的 snapshot/workdir 状态，但不再拥有第二套取消入口。

Real Electron smoke has exercised cancelled streaming, FFmpeg, MSE track merge, HLS and DASH staged outputs through the production publisher and verified target/partial/lease cleanup; real library delivery plus other FFmpeg entry points remain second-phase host evidence.

capabilities.notes: `StagedOutputLeaseStore` provides a main-only opaque lease base with owner-scoped paths, one delivery claim, TTL touch/reap, release cleanup and one-time startup readiness. `configureSession()` starts `ensureReady()` before the first output, which quarantines only `output-lease-*` directories left by a previous process and reaps expired entries; normal controller disposal releases every still-registered staged or claimed lease after active processing settles. Direct quarantine is refused while an in-process lease exists and unknown root entries remain untouched. `staged-output-publisher.ts#publishStagedOutput` owns the ordinary direct-file, captured-resource, HLS/MPD direct-manifest, HLS local-plan, HLS independent-track merge, HLS live stop-export, DASH static plan, DASH live stop-export, captured-resource transcode, and manual MSE resource merge handoffs: processing writes only to the lease path, then a single claim publishes to the user target while preserving the existing final `outputPath` response. Manual file-backed captured-resource output now passes the tab-scoped AbortSignal into its stream writer, so cancellation interrupts the copy rather than waiting for the entire source before lease cleanup. Real Electron smoke verifies that an in-flight manual MSE track merge releases its staged lease and leaves no target after tab-scoped cancellation. Lease paths and claim tokens intentionally do not cross IPC; renderer/import terminals remain owned by their domain adapters. Active DASH/HLS recorder workdirs remain process-local session resources and are cleaned by their lifecycle owners. Durable cross-process live continuation is an optional platform enhancement, not a fixed-target parity gap.

capabilities.notes: `CapturedOutputWorkflowCoordinator` now owns the application-scoped browser-download queue and one native download subscription. A library-detail listener can unmount and remount without losing completed MSE/native outputs, duplicate completion events are ignored, and failed/cancelled files are cleaned even when no workspace is mounted. Completed queue metadata is persisted in a versioned renderer journal with a 24-hour age bound; app/renderer restart rehydrates only valid completed downloads and resets any in-flight status to `pending`. Auth-session clear removes the journal, cleans non-active queued staging files, and ignores late completion events from the old session until a new session listener mounts; an active delivery reaches its own terminal cleanup. Delivery status remains `pending/importing/saving` until the existing UploadManager batch or local-save operation reaches a terminal result; failed/cancelled delivery returns to pending without deleting the file, success performs the single cleanup and removes the item, and concurrent delivery attempts for one download are rejected. `cat-catch:smoke-host` proves the native download/main journal/replacement renderer/save IPC/cleanup composition in a real isolated Electron process, and `cat-catch:smoke-large-host` repeats that chain with a deterministic 64 MiB file verified by streaming SHA-256. Frozen library targets and main-side restart cleanup have contract evidence; full authenticated-app crash recovery, real library delivery, multi-GiB media and long-wall-clock runs remain host-verification gaps.

capabilities.notes: `CapturedOutputWorkflowCoordinator.linkUploadTask` now owns the association between a queued browser output and an UploadManager batch promise. Upload completion remains visible after a renderer view unmounts; a successful batch performs the existing owned-file cleanup, while a failed or cancelled batch returns the output to `pending` for retry. Upload delivery consumes an explicit batch terminal classification (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `unknown`) and freezes `libraryId`, `parentId`, file name and relative path at batch creation so a later workspace/library switch cannot retarget the upload. The queue journal survives renderer/app restart, but an in-flight UploadManager batch is intentionally reset to `pending` and must be retried explicitly. The remaining gap is real production-host confirmation against a non-first library, not another target-freezing implementation.

capabilities.notes: `cat-catch-port/shared/output-helpers.ts#OutputHelpers` owns the Cat Catch filename filter/stringModify vocabulary, URL basename fallback, template variable and pipe evaluation, date/file variables, large ArrayBuffer-to-Blob chunking, and data-URL descriptor. It has no Electron, filesystem or renderer side effects; output services retain platform-safe path and delivery policy. The pinned template and large-buffer contracts are covered by executable target tests; consumers remain thin platform adapters.

`LocalSaveDeliveryAdapter` is the renderer-facing target owner for captured-resource local-save terminal projection. It delegates dialog, main-owned staging, filesystem write and cleanup to the existing Electron API, preserves the legacy `{ ok, cancelled, error, outputPath }` result, and adds a stable `terminal` classification (`completed`/`cancelled`/`failed`). The adapter is used by `useEmbeddedBrowserCatchToolkit`; durable recovery, real Electron save-dialog smoke and full output-integration closure remain open.

capabilities.notes: Normal BrowserWindow download completion and optional library import now use `DownloadHandoff` as a thin renderer adapter over the application-scoped `CapturedOutputWorkflowCoordinator`; the coordinator owns the queue, one native download subscription, delivery status and owned-file cleanup across listener unmount/remount. Completed metadata survives a renderer/app restart within the staging TTL; main initialization prunes expired, missing, or unsafe handoff records before any renderer replay, while auth-session clear removes queued non-active staging files and isolates old-session events. Library import uses the shared UploadManager terminal adapter with a frozen delivery target. The fixed-target owner and automated startup-recovery contract are closed. `cat-catch:smoke-host` uses the real Electron `DownloadItem`, forced renderer termination, replacement renderer, production save IPC and terminal cleanup; `cat-catch:smoke-large-host` verifies the same path for 64 MiB without materializing the fixture or verifier input as one full buffer. The remaining gaps are the full authenticated application, OS save dialog, real library import, cross-platform host, multi-GiB media and long-wall-clock runs.

capabilities.notes: Manifest download and manifest track merge share a cancel-aware process runner: HLS calls register its AbortSignal with the tab/request owner, termination uses the cross-platform process-tree adapter, and aborted/non-zero tasks remove partial output. Every manifest input receives its own protocol whitelist and allowed-extension policy before its input declaration, so a second encrypted track can resolve its local key instead of inheriting ffmpeg's default extension rejection. Conditional real-binary integrations verify probeable MP4/AAC output from generated local HLS and AES-128 encrypted fMP4/H264 plus independent AES-128/AAC tracks. Resource merge/transcode, DASH local-file merge and media-tool operations use the same executor and output contract; protocol tasks are registered with the application-wide ProcessingTaskRegistry and app shutdown disposes that registry, while executable probing remains a separate short-lived process. The real Electron host smoke now starts realtime lavfi through the production executor, cancels its tab-scoped outer task after a fragmented MP4 partial appears, and verifies AbortError plus process-tree/target/partial/lease/registry cleanup; absence of a discoverable FFmpeg is reported as `supported=false`, and this one path does not stand in for every FFmpeg caller.

capabilities.notes: Pinned upstream Base64-encodes m3u8dl custom-protocol payloads when configured. The production ExternalToolDispatcher accepts only tabId, opaque resourceId, and toolKey, redeems URL/metadata/protected headers from the main-owned Store/Vault, and rejects invalid, cross-tab, or stale requests before execution. The protocol adapter exposes an opt-in `encodePayload` setting that Base64-encodes the complete template payload after its scheme delimiter, preserving the default plain custom-protocol behavior. The local command executor keeps spawned commands registered until their real process exit, supports graceful-then-force tree termination during app shutdown, and preserves the fast dispatch return behavior. Options import/export is a separate peripheral Base64 consumer and remains outside this initial runtime mapping.
